demo.introBeforeLink: Iron Verdict allows judges to pick the reason for an invalid lift, shared instantly with athletes, audience, jury, and fellow judges. Available reasons are based on the
demo.athletes: Know your mistake immediately, no time wasted, and fix it on your next attempt.
demo.audience: No more guessing why a lift was ruled invalid.
demo.jury: Know exactly which part of the lift to review before voting.
demo.setupStep1: Enter a session name → click Create New Session
demo.setupStep2: Send the session code to other judges or scan QR code
demo.setupStep3: Use the session code to set up a Display Screen
demo.showReasonsDesc: Show reasons on display — ruling reasons appear on the display screen (enabled by default)
demo.requireReasonsDesc: Require reasons — judges must choose a reason before locking in (optional by default)
demo.liftCategoryDesc: Lift category dropdown — changes the reason catalogue (Squat / Bench / Deadlift)
demo.duringStep1: Head judge announces "The bar is loaded" and presses Start Timer
demo.duringStep2: After the lift, judges press their color, optionally pick a reason, then press Lock In
demo.duringStep3: When all three judges lock in, the result appears on the Display Screen
demo.duringStep4: Head judge presses Next Lift to reset for the next attempt
demo.duringStep5: If needed, head judge presses Reset Timer
demo.duringStep6: After the event: End Session → confirm with OK
demo.judgeImageAlt: Head judge screen on a phone: yellow chosen, reason “Skipped signal” selected, Lock In not yet pressed
demo.judgeImageCaption: Judge screen: pick a colour and a reason, then lock in
demo.resultImageAlt: Display screen showing a no lift: two red lights and one white, below them the cards with the reasons
demo.resultImageCaption: Display after a no lift: lights, cards and reasons
demo.displayCustomize: The display can be customised: gear icon top left → Edit layout. Move, resize or hide blocks. More under the “?” in the display settings.
demo.pauseNote: Breaks: Start break in the display settings – for all displays, as a countdown or until a time of day. More under the “?” in the display settings.
demo.livestream: For live streams there is a stream overlay for OBS: role selection → Stream overlay (OBS). More under the “?” there.
demo.editorImageAlt: Display screen in the layout editor: dashed frames around the blocks, toolbar with Save and Cancel, the timer hidden
demo.editorImageCaption: Layout editor: blocks framed, timer hidden
demo.popupNote: This demo is designed for desktop — it opens four pop-up windows to simulate three judges and a display running in parallel. Please allow pop-ups if prompted.
demo.demoRunning: Demo running — interact with the four open windows
demo.popupsBlockedAll: The pop-up windows were blocked. Allow pop-ups for this site and launch the demo again.
demo.popupsBlockedSome: Not all windows could be opened — pop-ups were blocked. Either allow pop-ups for this site and launch the demo again, or click “DEMO” in the top right of an open window to switch between screens.

overlay.layoutUrlInvalid: Layout code in the URL is invalid – saved layout in use
overlay.linkHint: Add this URL in OBS as a browser source (1920 × 1080). It opens the display without controls on a transparent background.

sections.title: Opening the settings
items: The gear in the top left corner or the S key opens and closes this panel, Esc closes it.
The stream overlay has no gear: there only the S key opens the panel (in OBS: right-click the source → Interact).
Layout and contrast mode apply to this device only and survive a reload. The break applies to every display of the session.

sections.title: Break (all displays)
items: Starts a break on every display of the session: for a number of minutes (countdown) or until a time of day.
Optionally set the next lift – the display then shows “Next: …”.
The break ends by itself when the time is up, as soon as the chief referee starts the timer, or with “End break”.
“Sending…” shows until the server confirmed the break. Without a connection the break cannot be controlled.

sections.title: Edit layout
items: “Edit layout” opens the editor. Drag a block to move it, drag its corner to resize it.
The handle beside the lights sets the gap between the lights.
“Hide” / “Show” on each block hides it or shows it again, e.g. the timer.
Changes apply only with “Save”. “Cancel” drops them, “Reset to default” brings back the default arrangement (stored with “Save”).
Lifter and attempt show sample data in the editor; during a competition they only appear in VPortal sessions.

sections.title: Layout code (export / import)
items: In the editor, “Layout code” shows the code of the current layout (IV1.…) to copy.
On another display: open the editor, “Layout code”, paste the code, “Apply”, then “Save”.

sections.title: Contrast mode
items: For bright halls: full colours instead of gradients, a clear border around the lights, whiter and bolder text. The background stays black.

sections.title: 1. Copy the URL
items: Open “Stream overlay (OBS)” and copy the URL. It contains the session code – use it on the streaming PC only; it is never visible in the stream.

sections.title: 2. Add the browser source
items: OBS → Sources → + → Browser.
URL: the copied URL. Width 1920, height 1080 (other sizes work too; keep the aspect ratio of your stream).
Leave Custom CSS empty. Leave “Shutdown source when not visible” off, so the overlay stays connected.
Put the source above the camera in the source list.

The overlay connects by itself and counts as one display. After an OBS restart, a reload of the source or a connection loss it reconnects on its own; while the connection is down, a small dot shows in the top right corner.
If the overlay shows “Session ended” or “Session not found”: enter the URL of the new session in the source.

sections.title: 3. Arrange the overlay
items: The overlay has its own layout, separate from the hall display.
A – directly in OBS: right-click the source → Interact → S key → “Edit layout”, arrange the blocks, hide those you do not need, “Save”. The layout is stored in OBS's browser profile.

B – prepare in a browser: open the overlay URL in Chrome, full screen (F11) on a 16:9 monitor, S → “Edit layout”, arrange, “Layout code” and copy the code (IV1.…). Append it to the URL in OBS: &layout=IV1.… Then only this layout applies; to change it, repeat B with the new code. This way the same layout works on another PC or at the next competition.
If the code in the URL is invalid, the overlay uses its saved (or the default) layout and the panel says so.
Do not stack blocks: their dark panels are translucent. Leave room around the lights for long reasons (two or three lines).

sections.title: Visible in the stream
items: The editor (with checkerboard and frames), the settings panel and the connect dialog show in the stream while they are open – set up before going live or hide the source meanwhile.

sections.title: VPortal (lifter and attempt info)
items: In VPortal sessions the overlay needs its own login, because OBS has its own browser profile: Interact → S → “Connect to comp software”. The login stays stored in the OBS profile.
Lifter and attempt info appear within a few seconds; after a reload the panel shows “Connected to … · <platform>”.

sections.title: Checklist before going live
items: Source 1920 × 1080, above the camera
A test vote shows the lights and the verdict in the preview, the background is transparent
Layout arranged (A or B), no blocks on top of each other, checkerboard gone (editor closed)
VPortal sessions: lifter and attempt info visible
Right-click → “Refresh cache of current page”: the overlay comes back by itself

sections.title: What for
items: The display shows name, club and class of the current lifter plus lift, attempt and weight – straight from VPortal, for the chosen stage.
Iron Verdict only reads. The scorekeeper still records the verdicts in VPortal.

sections.title: Federation and credentials
items: Federation: BVDK (Germany) or ÖVK (Austria), depending on which VPortal the competition was set up in.
Username and password of a VPortal account for this competition – the same as for logging in on the VPortal website.
The credentials are only passed on to VPortal to log in and are not stored on the Iron Verdict server.

sections.title: Stage
items: After logging in, choose the stage whose lifters this display should show. With several stages, each display connects to its own.

sections.title: One login per device
items: The login only applies to this device and this session. Every display that should show lifter data connects itself: a hall display on role select, before it switches to the display.
The stream overlay needs its own login because OBS has its own browser profile: in OBS Interact → key S → “Connect to comp software”.
After a reload the display keeps showing the lifter data. A reloaded hall display asks for the login again in the dialog, though; a new login replaces the stored one. A new session needs a new login.

sections.title: Visible in the stream
items: In the stream overlay this dialog is visible in the stream while it is open – including the username you type (the password stays hidden). Connect before going live or hide the source meanwhile.

sections.title: Problems and disconnecting
items: Lights, timer and verdicts keep working without VPortal.
If the connection to VPortal drops, the display shows “VPortal disconnected”; the lifter data is missing until it arrives again or you reconnect.
Disconnect: open this dialog again and choose “Disconnect”; this removes the login from this device. On a reloaded hall display the dialog offers no “Disconnect”.
